entry: Armed conflict in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], 1992–95, part of the [[Breakup of Yugoslavia|breakup of Yugoslavia]]. Bosnian Serb forces, led and supplied by [[Serbia]], seized approximately 70% of the country's territory in a campaign of ethnic cleansing. Atrocities were committed mainly by Serb forces and, to a lesser extent, by Croat and Bosniak forces. The [[Sarajevo|siege of Sarajevo]] and the Srebrenica massacre became emblematic. Over 8,000 Bosniak males were killed at Srebrenica in July 1995, the only incident in Europe recognized as [[Genocide|genocide]] since World War II. Peace negotiations in [[Dayton, Ohio]] produced the Dayton Accords, initialed on November 21, 1995. Estimates suggest over 100,000 people were killed.

Class of subatomic particles with integer spin. [[Fermion|Fermions]], which have half-integer spin, are the other fundamental class of subatomic particle, and every observed particle belongs to one of the two. Some bosons are elementary force carriers: the [[Photon|photon]] mediates the electromagnetic force, gluons mediate the strong force, and the W and Z bosons mediate the weak force. The [[Higgs boson]] contributes to the phenomenon of mass. Composite bosons include [[Meson|mesons]] and stable nuclei with even numbers of fermions. Identical bosons obey Bose–Einstein statistics, which places no limit on how many occupy one quantum state. [[Satyendra Nath Bose]] and [[Albert Einstein]] developed these statistics in the 1920s. Near absolute zero, helium-4 gas becomes a [[Superfluidity|superfluid]], and [[Bose–Einstein condensate|Bose–Einstein condensates]] extend this behavior to macroscopic scales.

Narrow strait in northwestern [[Turkey]]. The Bosporus connects the [[Black Sea]] to the [[Sea of Marmara]] and forms one of the continental boundaries between [[Europe]] and Asia. It is the world's narrowest strait used for international navigation. Its shores are heavily settled, especially in [[Istanbul]], whose metropolitan population is 17 million. The strait is about 31 km long and varies in width from 700 m to 3.7 km. Under the 1936 Montreux Convention, commercial vessels pass freely in peacetime, while Turkey may restrict warships. The Bosporus and the [[Dardanelles]] together are known as the Turkish Straits.

Relaxed style of [[Samba|samba]] developed in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil, in the late 1950s and early 1960s. Its calm syncopated rhythm, played on guitar with fingerstyle technique, mimics the beat of a samba school band. João Gilberto is credited with extracting the "bossa beat" from traditional samba. A common misconception holds that its unusual chords came from [[Jazz|jazz]], but samba guitarists had used similar structures since the early 1920s. Many bossa nova songs are now jazz standards. The album *Chega de Saudade* (1959), by Gilberto with compositions by Antônio Carlos Jobim, marked the first major recording of the style. *Getz/Gilberto* (1964), which included the hit "The Girl from Ipanema," brought bossa nova to international audiences and won multiple [[Grammy Awards]].

[[National Basketball Association]] team based in [[Boston]]. Founded in 1946 as one of the league's original eight teams, the Celtics play at TD Garden. The franchise holds the NBA record for championships, with 18, including eight consecutive titles from 1959 to 1966 under coach Red Auerbach and center [[Bill Russell]]. Its rivalry with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] was especially pronounced in the 1960s and 1980s, when [[Larry Bird]] led the team to three titles. Later championships came in 2008 and 2024.

[[Major League Baseball]] franchise based in [[Boston]]. Founded in 1901 as one of the American League's eight charter franchises, the team has played at Fenway Park since 1912. It won the first [[World Series]] in 1903 and nine World Series championships overall. The sale of [[Babe Ruth]] to the [[New York Yankees]] was followed by an 86-year championship drought, dubbed the "Curse of the Bambino," which ended in 2004. The rivalry with the Yankees is among the fiercest in North American professional sports. "Sweet Caroline" by [[Neil Diamond]] has become one of the team's anthems.

Protest in [[Boston]], Massachusetts, against British taxation, on December 16, 1773. Disguised as American Indians, members of the Sons of Liberty dumped 340 or 342 chests of [[Tea|tea]] from [[East India Company]] ships into Boston Harbor. The protest opposed the Tea Act of 1773, which let the East India Company sell tea in the colonies without taxes beyond those of the Townshend Acts. Parliament responded with the Intolerable Acts of 1774, which ended local self-government in Massachusetts and closed Boston's commercial port. The Battles of Lexington and Concord in April 1775 launched the [[American Revolutionary War]].

City (pop., 2020: 675,647), capital of [[Massachusetts]]. Boston was founded in 1630 by English [[Puritans|Puritan]] settlers on the Shawmut Peninsula, who named it after the market town of Boston, Lincolnshire, England. It was a center of the [[American Revolution]], site of the Boston Massacre (1770), the [[Boston Tea Party]] (1773), and the Battle of Bunker Hill (1775). The city's firsts include Boston Common, the nation's first public park (1634), and the Tremont Street subway (1897), the first subway system in the nation. By the 21st century it had become a global leader in higher education and research, with [[Harvard University]] and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] among its institutions. The city is the largest biotechnology hub in the world. Its economy is led by finance, professional and business services, information technology, and government. The Greater Boston metropolitan area had 5 million people in 2025.

Parasitic [[Fly|fly]] of the family Oestridae, also known as warble fly, heel fly, or gadfly. Botfly [[Larva|larvae]] live inside [[Mammal|mammals]], infesting the [[Skin|skin]], digestive tract, or nasal passages of their hosts. Cattle, sheep, goats, horses, and [[Reindeer]] are common hosts, and infestation can cause irritation, weight loss, and secondary infections. Adult females deposit eggs on hosts or on vectors such as mosquitoes and [[Tick|ticks]]. Development in the host takes 4–12 weeks. Humans are rarely infested, and *Dermatobia hominis*, the human botfly of Central and South America, is the only species known to parasitize humans routinely.

Landlocked country in [[Southern Africa|southern Africa]] (pop., 2025: 2.5 million). About 70% of its territory is part of the [[Kalahari Desert]], and its capital and largest city is [[Gaborone]]. Britain declared a protectorate, Bechuanaland, in 1885. The country became independent under its present name on September 30, 1966, and has since been a parliamentary republic with uninterrupted democratic elections. The Botswana Democratic Party governed until 2024, when the Umbrella for Democratic Change won the general election. Tourism and mining dominate the economy, and Botswana produces more diamonds than any country except [[Russia]]. Unemployment, severe income inequality, and one of the world's most critical [[HIV/AIDS]] epidemics remain serious problems. Botswana is a member of the [[Commonwealth of Nations]].

Heavy third-generation [[Elementary particle|elementary particle]], one of the six quarks, with electric charge −1/3 e. Also called the b or beauty quark, it was discovered in 1977 at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory through the Υ meson, a bound state of a bottom quark and its antiquark. Its transitions to lower-mass quarks are exceptionally rare. The bottom quark is a product of almost all top quark decays and a frequent decay product of the [[Higgs boson]].

Neurotoxic protein produced by *Clostridium botulinum*, considered the deadliest known substance produced naturally in recorded chemical literature. It prevents the release of acetylcholine at nerve endings, causing flaccid paralysis and [[Botulism]]. The seven main types are named A to G, and types A and B cause disease in humans. Developed as a biological weapon by Soviet, United States, and Iraqi programs, the toxin is used in strongly diluted form for medical and cosmetic purposes. The estimated median lethal dose of type A toxin is 1.3–2.1 ng/kg intravenously or intramuscularly.

Rare, potentially fatal illness caused by [[Botulinum toxin|botulinum toxin]] produced by *Clostridium botulinum*. It begins with weakness, blurred vision, fatigue, and trouble speaking, and may progress to weakness of the arms, chest, and legs. It usually does not affect consciousness or cause fever. Foodborne, infant, and wound botulism are the main forms; infant botulism usually affects children under one year old. The disease is not passed directly between people. Heating the toxin above 85 °C (185 °F) for more than five minutes destroys it, but not the spores. [[Honey]] can contain the organism, so it should not be fed to children under 12 months. Treatment uses antitoxin, and [[Antibiotic|antibiotics]] may be used for wound botulism. Death occurs in 5 to 10% of people. The name derives from [[Latin]] *botulus*, meaning sausage.

Queen of the Iceni, an ancient British tribe. Her husband, Prasutagus, had ruled as a nominally independent ally of [[Roman Empire|Rome]] and left his kingdom jointly to his daughters and the emperor. After his death the will was ignored, the kingdom was annexed, and, according to the Roman historian [[Tacitus]], Boudica was flogged and her daughters raped. In AD 60 or 61 she led the Iceni and other tribes in a revolt that destroyed Camulodunum (modern Colchester), Londinium (London), and Verulamium, killing an estimated 70,000–80,000 Romans and Britons. The governor Gaius Suetonius Paulinus defeated the rebels, and Boudica died shortly afterwards, by suicide or illness. The crisis led [[Nero]] to consider withdrawing all imperial forces from Britain. Interest in her was revived in the English [[Renaissance]], and she became a British national heroine and cultural symbol in the [[Victorian era]].

Main island of the [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville]], part of [[Papua New Guinea]]. Bougainville is the largest island in the [[Solomon Islands]] archipelago, covering 9,384 sq km. Mount Balbi rises to 2,715 m. Copper and gold were mined at Panguna, and the Bougainville crisis, a secessionist conflict from 1988 to 1998, caused an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 deaths. A 2019 referendum voted for independence from Papua New Guinea, but the vote was non-binding on its government. A timeline set out in July 2026 provides for self-government from 2027 to 2030 and independence on September 1, 2030.

Genus of thorny ornamental vines, shrubs, and trees in the family Nyctaginaceae. Native to tropical forests of [[South America]], including Brazil, Colombia, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and Argentina, the plants bear large colorful bracts that surround three simple waxy flowers. The bracts make the genus popular as an ornamental. It is named after the explorer Louis Antoine de Bougainville, who documented it on one of his expeditions.

Social class of business owners, merchants, and other wealthy people. It emerged in the Late Middle Ages as a "[[Middle class|middle class]]" between the [[Peasant|peasantry]] and the aristocracy, and its original urban sense was closely tied to [[Liberalism|liberalism]]. In Marxist theory, the bourgeoisie owns the means of production and extracts surplus value from the labor of the proletariat within [[Capitalism|capitalism]]. According to Marxists, the bourgeoisie will eventually be overthrown, and it would cease to exist in a classless society.

Coastal resort town in Dorset, England. The area was uninhabited heathland until Lewis Tregonwell founded a health resort there in 1810. The Ringwood, Christchurch and Bournemouth Railway, which opened in 1870, turned the town into a major resort that attracts over 5 million visitors a year. Its seven-mile stretch of golden sand draws visitors, and the town centre is notable for its Victorian architecture. Financial services now play a significant role alongside tourism. The town is home to AFC Bournemouth, a [[Premier League]] club.

Uninhabited subantarctic volcanic island and dependency of [[Norway]]. A nature reserve in the [[Atlantic Ocean|South Atlantic Ocean]], it is the world's most remote island, and most of its 49 sq km is covered by [[Glacier|glacier]]. The French explorer Jean-Baptiste Charles Bouvet de Lozier first sighted it on January 1, 1739. A Norwegian expedition landed and claimed it in 1927, and it was declared a Norwegian dependency in 1930. It was designated a nature reserve in 1971.

Family of cloven-hoofed [[Ruminant|ruminant]] mammals, including [[Cattle]], bison, antelopes, [[Sheep]], and goats. There are 143 extant species and 300 known extinct species. All male bovids have two or more horns, apart from some domesticated forms, and in many species females have horns too. Each horn is an unbranched bony core covered by a permanent keratin sheath. The earliest known bovid evolved by 20 million years ago, in the early [[Miocene]]. Bovids are most diverse in Africa, especially in the savannas of eastern Africa. Cattle, sheep, and goats are domesticated bovids whose use has spread worldwide, providing milk, cheese, leather, meat, and wool.

Fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle, known as mad cow disease. It is thought to be caused by a [[Prion|prion]], an infectious misfolded protein, and it is incurable and always fatal. Symptoms include abnormal behavior, trouble walking, and weight loss, and death follows weeks to months after onset. Cattle are believed to have been infected by feed containing meat-and-bone meal. The [[United Kingdom|UK]] experienced an outbreak in the 1980s and 1990s, with more than 184,000 cattle diagnosed from 1986 to 2015. Spread to humans is believed to cause [[Variant Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease|variant Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease]]. In the UK, animals older than 30 months may not enter the human food or animal feed supply.

Ranged weapon system consisting of an elastic bow and long-shafted projectiles, the arrows. Humans used bows for [[Hunting|hunting]] and aggression long before recorded history. They were important weapons of war from ancient history until the [[Early modern period|early modern period]], when [[Firearm|firearms]] made them increasingly obsolete. The earliest direct evidence of bow use dates to about 64,000 years ago at Sibudu Cave in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Bows are now used mainly for sport and hunting. [[Archery]] is the art of shooting arrows with a bow, and a bowyer is someone who makes bows.

Baleen whale of [[Arctic]] and subarctic waters, the only living member of the genus *Balaena*. Also called the Greenland right whale, it is named for its massive triangular skull, which it uses to break through Arctic ice. Its mouth is nearly one-third of its body length, and its baleen plates are the longest among whales, with a maximum length of 2.97 to 5.2 m. Bowheads may be the longest-lived mammals, reaching more than 200 years. Early [[Whaling]] reduced populations severely until a 1966 moratorium. The global population is of least concern on the IUCN Red List.

Target sport in which a player rolls a ball toward pins or another target. Most references to bowling mean pin bowling, especially [[Tenpin bowling|tenpin bowling]], which is played in the United Kingdom, the Commonwealth, and elsewhere. Target bowling includes lawn bowls. Bowling is played by 120 million people in more than 90 countries. In tenpin bowling a game consists of 10 frames, and a perfect game of 300 requires 12 consecutive strikes.

Class of [[Cnidaria|cnidarian]] animals with cube-shaped medusae. Some species produce [[Venom|venom]] that is extremely painful and often fatal to humans. Stings from *Chironex fleckeri*, *Carukia barnesi*, and *Malo kingi* are among the most dangerous, while *Carybdea murrayana* causes a painful sting that is not fatal. Box jellyfish are agile predators that catch small fish and crustaceans with tentacles armed with nematocysts, or stinging cells. The lineage dates back at least 300 million years.
